title: Q-SENTINEL
items:
Intelligent QRNG Reliability, Forensics
& Early-Warning System
Ashin R   /   Akhash A   /   Anushek RK   /   Astlin Dijo D   /   Aravind R
WO-012   Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) Entropy Validator
Continuous monitoring. Evidence engineers can investigate.
notes: Opening, 30 seconds. Introduce the team and problem WO-012. A QRNG uses quantum measurements as a randomness source. Q-Sentinel examines its digitized output and helps engineers investigate changes. Our prototype uses files and classical simulated streams. Team 55, Gladiators. Members: Ashin R, Akhash A, Anushek RK, Astlin Dijo D, Aravind R. Source: user-supplied six-slide outline and q-sentinel/README.md.

title: Randomness can degrade silently
items:
The quantum source is only part of the pipeline.
Acquisition and processing can introduce unwanted patterns.

Unpredictable numbers support
cryptographic keys, authentication
and secure communications.

When did the change appear?
What changed, and how severely?
What should we investigate?
Our focus: detect persistent changes early and explain the evidence.
notes: About 45 seconds. Noise, bit bias, dependence, detector operating conditions, acquisition timing and post-processing can affect observed output. These are possible contributors, not diagnoses from bits alone. A pass/fail statistical summary is useful but does not itself explain the timeline. Avoid claiming all existing tools lack monitoring. Early detection is an objective evaluated in simulations, not a guarantee for every fault. Source: user outline, q-sentinel/README.md.

title: A warning linked to its statistical evidence
items:
Windowed entropy and
six NIST test families
track the stream over time.

An entropy fingerprint
shows changes in bias,
dependence and patterns.

Q-Advisor explains alerts
and suggests checks.
A passport saves the record.
DATA → WINDOWS → MEASURE → DETECT → EXPLAIN → RECOMMEND
Failure Lab: inject known faults and inspect the resulting evidence.
Conditional forecasts appear only when a consistent trend supports them.
notes: About 55 seconds. Entropy fingerprinting combines normalized anomalies and raw metrics such as marginal Shannon/min entropy, bias, correlation, runs and spectral characteristics. Rule-based signatures describe behavior consistent with bias, correlation, periodicity, bursts or repetition. They do not prove hardware causes. The Failure Lab supports controlled faults. Forecasts are conditional projections and may be unavailable. The added value is connecting monitoring, first-detection evidence and engineering follow-up. Sources: user outline; q-sentinel/README.md.

title: One analysis pipeline, explainable decisions
items:
Shannon / min entropy
Bias / autocorrelation
Runs / spectral behavior

Six NIST SP 800-22 families
P-values and applicability
Window-level evidence

Calibrated CUSUM
Rule-based signatures
Health score / Q-Advisor
Dashboard and reports preserve the measurements behind each alert.
Python / Streamlit / NumPy / Pandas / SciPy / Plotly / SQLite
Classical simulation is labeled. Q-Advisor uses rules, not a trained AI model.
notes: About 65 seconds. Inputs currently include TXT, CSV and binary files plus the simulator. CUSUM accumulates deviations from a frozen baseline, with calibration and persistence rules. An initial 30-window baseline is unverified unless supplied reference data is available. Six NIST families: Frequency, Block Frequency, Runs, Longest Run, DFT and Cumulative Sums forward/backward. Marginal entropy does not capture all sequence predictability. NIST passes do not certify quantum origin or security. SQLite stores history, and ReportLab produces PDF reports. Serial, TCP/WebSocket and MQTT adapters remain future integration points. Sources: q-sentinel/README.md; NIST SP 800-22 Rev.1a https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/22/r1/upd1/final.

title: A working prototype with a clear pilot path
items:
Local analysis, simulated faults,
forensic bit inspection and reports.
No quantum hardware or paid API
is needed for the demonstration.

71 of 75 fault scenarios detected
4 misses; 2 false alerts / 350 healthy windows

1   Pilot with real QRNG recordings
2   Validate hardware adapters
3   Assess continuous deployment

AWS EC2 / Linux / Docker
Deployment and cost validation remain.
Simulation results do not establish performance on physical QRNG hardware.
notes: About 60 seconds. The MVP runs on a Windows laptop using mature Python libraries. The digital twin is an engineering-level classical simulation, not quantum physics simulation. Evaluation used five seeds and 75 fault scenarios; 71 were detected and 4 missed. There were 2 false alert events over 350 healthy monitoring windows. Do not describe 71/75 as overall accuracy. Early-warning comparison had 16 earlier detections, 41 simultaneous, 3 later and 15 without jointly available times. Do not claim every fault is found before NIST. A real-data lab pilot is required. AWS EC2, Linux and Docker are proposed deployment targets, not verified current deployments. Actual costs depend on resources and usage. Sources: q-sentinel/output/evaluation-summary.json; q-sentinel/VALIDATION.md; user outline.

title: A clearer investigation for QRNG engineers
items: Find persistent changes and the first flagged window.
Show statistical signatures and conditional trends.
Guide investigation and preserve a health passport.
For QRNG researchers, device engineers and security laboratories.
When did it change? What is the evidence? What should we check?
Statistical analysis alone cannot establish quantum origin or cryptographic security.
notes: Closing, about 45 seconds. Potential application areas include QRNG development for cryptographic key generation, secure communication, authentication, quantum networks and research. These are intended use areas, not current customers or certified production deployments. First detection is not necessarily the true physical onset. Trend projections require sufficient consistent evidence and are conditional. The next milestone is validation against real QRNG recordings and hardware measurements. End with: Q-Sentinel helps engineers understand when randomness changes, what evidence supports the warning, and what to investigate next. Offer the Failure Lab demo, using actual displayed values rather than promising an alert order. Sources: user outline; q-sentinel/README.md.
